_meta.description: Hypothesis register. Each hypothesis states a falsifiable prediction, the exact test executed, and the verbatim evidence returned. 'supported'/'refuted' describe the evidence gathered in this session only.
_meta.reverification_note: 2026-09-16 audit pass: claims were narrowed to what the registered evidence tests. H4 now concludes only that volatility alone is insufficient; H5 no longer claims realization timing compounds P/L; H10 uses an exact timestamped snapshot; H12 is descriptive rather than causal.

hypotheses.claim: Returns of >=10x on the paper account are achievable in The Leap and have been officially recorded.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one completed edition has a published #1 net profit >= 900%.
hypotheses.test: Count records in data/verified_explosive_returns.json with return_multiple >= 10.
evidence: Completed Futures - February 2025: BenBernanke1, +5,220.72% (53.2072x), 59,187 participants.
Live AMP Futures - September 2026 snapshot: leonardo22_romano, +921.49% (10.2149x), 93,527 displayed participants; in progress and not a final result.

hypotheses.claim: In the captured official champion sample, records at or above 10x occur in futures editions; the two captured stock editions finished below 1.3x.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one completed futures record is at or above 10x, while both captured completed stock records are below 1.3x.
hypotheses.test: Group completed records in data/verified_explosive_returns.json by asset_class_label and compare their observed ranges. Do not infer causation or a universal strategy route.
evidence: Completed futures sample: best 53.2072x and at least one record above 10x.
Completed stocks sample (n=2): 1.299x and 1.1758x.
This small champion-only sample does not prove that leverage or asset class caused the difference.

hypotheses.claim: The live (September 2026) contest permits trading single stocks.
hypotheses.prediction: The permitted instrument list contains at least one NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX single-stock contract.
hypotheses.test: Parse data/contest_universe.json and count instruments whose exchange is an equity venue.
evidence: 94 instruments in the permitted list. Exchange breakdown: CBOT 17, CBOT_MINI 15, CME 24, CME_MINI 18, COMEX 5, COMEX_MINI 6, NYMEX 7, NYMEX_MINI 2. Equity instruments: 0.

hypotheses.claim: Per-unit volatility by itself is sufficient to identify the best instrument for absolute-dollar leaderboard placement.
hypotheses.prediction: If sufficient, no position-cap, multiplier, quote-price, or buying-power input would change the dollar P/L comparison.
hypotheses.test: Combine each selected instrument’s rules cap, verified multiplier, captured TradingView continuous-contract price, and the 20:1 initial buying-power limit. Compute whole-contract modeled notional and the favorable percentage move needed to equal the captured rank-250 P/L. Historical normalized volatility is not available, so do not rank expected returns.
evidence: Dollar P/L per underlying point equals contracts × multiplier; dollar P/L for a 1% move also depends on price.
At the captured prices, the 20:1 buying-power model reduces CL from its rules cap of 100 contracts to 48 whole contracts, SI from 25 to 15, HO from 25 to 23, and NQ from 100 to 8.
The favorable underlying moves needed to equal the captured rank-250 P/L are 12.6853% for CL, 12.8094% for SI, 12.9120% for HO, and 13.3236% for NQ under the stated model assumptions.

Conclusion is limited: volatility alone is insufficient. The repository has not measured normalized historical volatility and does not claim that caps, margin, or any one instrument is the binding or best predictor.

hypotheses.claim: The live rules rank participants by realized profit/loss on closed positions, and the public leaderboard displays both percentage and absolute-dollar columns.
hypotheses.prediction: The rules define realized P/L on closed positions as the ranking metric, and displayed dollars are consistent with displayed percentage on the 250,000 virtual-USD base.
hypotheses.test: Read the ranking clause and recompute captured leaderboard rows within the maximum error implied by percentage rounding.
evidence: Rules: 'A participant’s place ... is determined based on the realized profit/loss on the Competition account.'
Rules: realized P/L is P/L on closed positions; all open positions are automatically closed at the end and included.
The leaderboard displays 'Realized profit %' and 'Realized profit $'.
Snapshot rank 1: 250,000 × 9.2149 = 2,303,725, exactly the displayed realized P/L. Closing timing does not create extra P/L; it only changes when open P/L becomes realized.

hypotheses.claim: A return at or above 100x is present in the 16-record official contest sample captured by this repository.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one captured official record shows return_multiple >= 100.
evidence: 0 cases at or above 100x across all 16 sourced records.
The sample maximum is 53.2072x (Futures - February 2025). This does not prove a universal ceiling or exhaust every edition.

hypotheses.claim: Contest parameters are stable across editions, so a strategy tuned once carries over.
hypotheses.prediction: Balance, leverage, position caps and commission are identical between consecutive futures editions.
hypotheses.test: Diff the TradeStation Jul 2026 rules against the AMP Futures Sep 2026 rules.
evidence: Balance 100,000 -> 250,000 virtual USD (2.5x).
Futures leverage 10:1 -> 20:1 (2x); max notional 1,000,000 -> 5,000,000 (5x).
NYMEX:CL1! position cap 1.0 -> 100.0 contracts (100x).
CME:MBT1! position cap 5.0 -> 25.0 contracts (5x).
Prize-paying ranks 250 -> 300.

hypotheses.claim: A free-plan account can compete on equal terms in the live edition.
hypotheses.prediction: Free-plan participants receive the same market data as paid participants.
hypotheses.test: Read the real-time data clause (section 06) of the live rules.
evidence: Rules: free-plan users 'who were not previously active users of TradingView's paid services will not be provided with the Competition Real-Time Data by reason of their participation in the Competition.'
Rules: after subscribing, 'access to the Competition Real-Time Data will then be granted within twenty-four (24) hours'.
They may register and are prize-eligible, but they trade without competition real-time data unless they subscribe or trial.

hypotheses.claim: The leverage-implied upper bound on initial account notional is $5,000,000 before per-symbol caps and whole-contract constraints.
hypotheses.prediction: The starting balance multiplied by stated futures leverage equals $5,000,000.
hypotheses.test: Recompute starting_balance_virtual_usd × futures_leverage_ratio from the live rules.
evidence: 'The preset balance size for the Paper Trading Competition Account is 250,000 virtual USD. Leverage for futures: 20:1.'
Computed upper bound: 250,000 x 20 = 5,000,000 USD. Actual initial deployment can be lower because of position caps and whole-contract quantities.

Corollary (computed): an adverse move of 250,000 / 5,000,000 = 5.00% on a hypothetical fully deployed $5,000,000 notional equals the entire starting balance. Equivalently 1/20 = 5%, the inverse of the stated leverage.

hypotheses.claim: The captured live leaderboard frontiers are point-in-time values that move during the edition; at 2026-09-16T21:39:34Z, ranks 50, 100, and 250 displayed +457.64%, +384.08%, and +249.48%.
hypotheses.prediction: A later same-day capture can differ from an earlier capture because the rules allow leaderboard updates during the contest.
hypotheses.test: Compare data/live_contest_snapshot.json with the earlier same-day rows archived in research/evidence/TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026.md.
evidence: Tier boundaries: rank 25 +578.89%, rank 26 +569.30%, rank 50 +457.64%, rank 51 +454.33%.
Earlier same-day archived rank-250 values were lower, demonstrating snapshot drift.
The public page displays only ranks through 250 even though rules award up to 300 potential prizes; no public rank-300 threshold is claimed.

hypotheses.claim: The leaderboard's displayed $ profit equals 250,000 x (displayed %)/100 up to the rounding of the percentage to two decimals — the % and $ columns are one number, not two.
hypotheses.prediction: Every captured dollar value lies within $12.50 of 250,000 × displayed_pct/100, the maximum error caused by rounding percentage to two decimals.
hypotheses.test: Recompute all seven rows in data/live_contest_snapshot.json.
evidence: Every difference is within the inclusive $12.50 rounding bound.

hypotheses.claim: Winning returns vary substantially across the captured editions; this sample does not establish a universal win number or prove that asset class caused the difference.
hypotheses.prediction: The observed completed-champion range spans both sub-1.3x and above-10x outcomes.
hypotheses.test: Compare all completed #1 records in data/verified_explosive_returns.json by edition and asset-class label; exclude the in-progress live row from final-winner conclusions.
evidence: Captured completed stock champions: 1.1758x and 1.299x.
Captured completed futures champion maximum: 53.2072x.
Observed association is not causation: editions also differ in balance, leverage, caps, instruments, duration, and field behavior. No normalized volatility or causal model has been run.

hypotheses.claim: The brief's volatile-stock list is a historical research reference for future stock-edition work, not an actionable instrument set in the live futures contest; future eligibility must be rechecked.
hypotheses.prediction: Every one of the 20 stock records cites market_data_vendor sources only, and none of those 20 symbols appears in the 94-instrument permitted universe of the live September 2026 edition.
hypotheses.test: Inspect the source tier of every record in data/volatile_stocks.json and intersect its symbols against data/contest_universe.json.
evidence: All 20 volatile_stocks.json records cite YAHOO-* market_data_vendor source_ids; scripts/verify.py forbids any non-vendor source for stock evidence (check_volatile_stocks.source_tier).

None of the 20 stock symbols (ENPH, AMD, MARA, CVNA, GME, RIOT, SHOP, NVAX, APP, PLUG, MSTR, NIO, PLTR, AMC, SMCI, HOOD, TSLA, NVDA, COIN, PTON) appears in contest_universe.json (94 futures instruments, 0 equities).

TradingView's official March 2026 Magnificent Seven stock-edition rules used a different, seven-stock NASDAQ universe. That confirms eligibility is edition-specific; it does not establish that this 20-stock list will be eligible later.

hypotheses.claim: A Donchian channel breakout with EMA-trend and ATR-expansion filters (model S1) earns a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars across the capturable contest universe.
hypotheses.prediction: Across non-overlapping 30-day walk-forward windows on every captured symbol with >=150 bars, the pooled median net profit is positive (>$0) at zero cost, survives removal of the best symbol and best window, and nearby channel lengths (15, 25) keep it positive.
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py (engine intel-1) simulated S1 on 10 captured symbols (210 windows, 2024-09-17 to 2026-09-17 vendor daily bars) per research/strategy/testing-plan.md; verdicts follow the pre-registered falsification rules.
evidence: Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 (mean $12,528.50 is driven by outliers); 15.24% of 210 windows were positive.
Only 70 closed trades total (43 long, 27 short); 3 of 210 windows reached >=5x (best: COMEX:SI1! 2025-12-08->2026-01-06, 7.39x on a single trade), 0 reached >=10x.
Concentration checks fail: excluding the best symbol or the best window flips the pooled median non-positive; per-symbol medians are $0 for all 10 symbols.
Sensitivity grid: channel_length 15 -> median $0.0 (75 trades), channel_length 25 -> median $0.0 (70 trades).
Worst window: NYMEX:NG1! 2026-01-07->2026-02-05 at -2.356x (margin breach without liquidation, per stated assumptions).

hypotheses.claim: An EMA impulse continuation entry (fast EMA crossing/holding above slow EMA with ATR expansion, model S2) earns a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars.
hypotheses.prediction: Pooled median net profit across all captured-symbol walk-forward windows is positive at zero cost and stays positive after moderate costs ($1.50/side + 5% ATR slippage) and at nearby EMA pairs (15x40, 25x60).
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py simulated S2 on the same 10 symbols / 210 windows with the pre-registered cost and sensitivity protocol.
evidence: Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 and the mean is negative (-$2,986.10); only 7.14% of windows were positive.
28 closed trades in 210 windows; 0 windows reached >=5x (best window CME_MINI:NQ1! 2025-02-11->2025-03-12 at 1.87x).
Moderate-cost median $0.0 (mean -$3,960.53); high-cost median $0.0 (mean -$4,932.10).
Sensitivity grid: ema15x40 -> median $0.0 (27 trades), ema25x60 -> median $0.0 (33 trades); concentration checks fail on symbol and window removal.

hypotheses.claim: Entering on a Bollinger-band squeeze release (bandwidth at a 50-bar low then expansion, model S3) captures the volatility expansions that follow squeezes, earning a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars.
hypotheses.prediction: Pooled median net profit across captured-symbol walk-forward windows is positive at zero cost, and the trade count is large enough for the declared bootstrap confidence interval.
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py simulated S3 on the same 10 symbols / 210 windows; squeeze-release signals on daily bars are rare, so the sample-size rule applies.
evidence: Only 4 closed trades in 210 windows (0.95% of windows positive); the pre-registered rule rejects a bootstrap CI on 4 trades.
Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 (mean $123.93); 0 windows reached >=5x (best NYMEX:NG1! 2026-06-17->2026-07-16 at 1.16x).
Sensitivity grid: band_length 15 -> median $0.0 (5 trades), band_length 25 -> median $0.0 (9 trades).
S3's signal is too rare on daily bars to be a leaderboard strategy inside 30-day windows; intraday data would be required to re-test it meaningfully.

hypotheses.claim: Within the capturable universe, the instruments whose historical 30-day moves most exceed the move needed to reach the rank-250 frontier are the full-size energy and metals contracts (CL1!, HO1!, RB1!, SI1!, PL1!), because their modeled initial notional hits the leverage cap, while micro contracts and ETH1! are structurally priced out.
hypotheses.prediction: Ranking captured symbols by (best 30-day up move) / (favorable move needed to reach the $623,689 rank-250 target from the modeled initial notional) puts full-size CL/HO/RB/SI/PL at the top, NG1! near the middle despite the highest volatility, and QM1!/ETH1! at the bottom.
hypotheses.test: data/volatility_intelligence.json (written by scripts/run_backtests.py alongside the backtests) computed annualized volatility, ATR(14), best 30-day up/down moves and the rank-250 requirement per symbol from the same vendor daily bars.
evidence: Needed vs delivered (favorable move needed -> best 30d up move): CL1! 12.7%->58.4%, HO1! 12.9%->78.2%, SI1! 12.8%->64.7%, RB1! 18.4%->66.7%, PL1! 27.9%->50.3% - each historically delivered 1.8x-6.1x its requirement.

NG1! is the most volatile symbol (87.5% annualized, best 30d up +140.4%, largest overnight gap 49.8%) but its margin-limited initial notional ($722,750) requires +86.3%, which its best move exceeds 1.6x.

QM1! needs +121.8% (micro contract, $512,125 notional) but only ever delivered +58.4%; ETH1! needs +517.7% ($120,475 notional at the capture price) but only ever delivered +71.8% - both flagged note_if_best_move_exceeds_rank250_requirement=false.

All values derive from market_data_vendor captures (YAHOO-FUTURES-CHART) and are simulation inputs, not predictions; the rank-250 target comes from the official leaderboard snapshot captured 2026-09-16T21:39:34Z via TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026.
